title: NETWORK_POLICY_ENFORCING_MODE set on aws-node without the aws-eks-nodeagent container fails every pod (v1.19.4+)

detection.reason: the rule asks whether the agent container is ABSENT while the env name is present; the vocabulary tests presence only

quote: Skip configuring NP related if network_policy_enforcing_mode is not set
remediation: From v1.19.4 the CNI plugin calls the Network Policy Agent on every pod ADD whenever NETWORK_POLICY_ENFORCING_MODE is non-empty (v1.19.3 did so only in strict mode). A raw-manifest aws-node that dropped the aws-eks-nodeagent container but kept NETWORK_POLICY_ENFORCING_MODE=standard then fails every pod sandbox with `add cmd: failed to setup network policy`. Remove the variable, or keep the agent container (the chart drops the variable for you when nodeAgent is disabled).
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get ds aws-node -o json | jq -r '[.spec.template.spec.containers[] | .name] as $n | [.spec.template.spec.containers[] | .env[]? | select(.name == "NETWORK_POLICY_ENFORCING_MODE") | .value] as $m | if (($m | length) != 0 and ($n | index("aws-eks-nodeagent") | not)) then "BROKEN: NETWORK_POLICY_ENFORCING_MODE=\($m[0]) without aws-eks-nodeagent" else "ok" end'  # BROKEN = every new pod fails to get a network on v1.19.4+
